Future: where Quantum Phantoms leads

Whole-pipeline outlook, written in INT (2026-10-29): cancer detection, other organs and body systems, the path toward a digital twin, predictions at 5 / 10 / 15 years, and the risks. Today's state is on the index and in the INT gap list.

How to read this page: every claim carries a label. evidence-based means a number in this repo or a cited paper code (PDFs in ../papers/). extrapolation means a reasoned step beyond that evidence. speculative means possible but not supported yet. Each letter's README has its own Future section for its paper(s); this page covers the pipeline as a whole.

1. Aim of the work

Quantum Phantoms generates synthetic lung tumours inside real 3-D chest CT, with every step reproducible and signed. The 21 reverse-engineering targets each rebuild one published method for one stage:

  1. Where a tumour sits inside the lung anatomy (A).
  2. What kind of tumour it is, drawn from cited statistics (B).
  3. How its randomness is certified by a Bell test (C).
  4. How it grows quantum-mechanically at the cell-fate level (D).
  5. How it grows as tissue between baseline and follow-up (E).
  6. How it looks on a scanner with that scanner's noise and blur (F).
  7. How it is traced back to its signed inputs (G).
  8. How it is validated against real patient scans (H).

Why it matters: AI that finds lung cancer on CT is trained and tested on scarce, unevenly labelled patient data. Synthetic tumours with exact ground truth, controlled difficulty and no patient voxels can fill the gaps, but only if they are realistic, traceable and validated. This project is about that credibility, not about security and not about quantum speed-ups.

2. Contribution

  • Reproduced methods. 13 targets are adapted and 6 dissected, and every one carries a published number checked against ours (index target table). Several honest non-matches are recorded: A #18, D #8, F #17, H R20b. evidence-based
  • One contract layer. 21 frozen contracts with stubs let every stage be built and tested alone, and the INT runner chains them through their own CLIs. evidence-based
  • A claim ladder for "quantum". L0 provenance, L1 entangled generative state, L1′ memory advantage; L2/L3 are out of reach today. Every quantum number ships its classical baseline and simulation label. evidence-based
  • Privacy by construction. Tumours are drawn from fitted parameters (about 4 KB of scalars from LIDC), never from patient voxels. This avoids the memorization risk of learned generators [H07, H08]. evidence-based
  • A weak-link map of the integrated chain (INT gap list): the three weakest edges are known and each has a fix. evidence-based

3. Role in cancer detection

Concrete end goal: a generator of certified, traceable synthetic lung-nodule CT cohorts, with baseline and follow-up, used to:

  1. Train detection and segmentation models on cases that real data under-represents: juxtapleural, tiny or ground-glass nodules (A, B, E, F). extrapolation
  2. Stress-test them per location, size, type, scanner and dose with exact masks, finding blind spots before patients do. extrapolation
  3. Measure growth assessment: reported vs true volume and doubling time on a commercial assistant, using H's #21 protocol with E's baseline/follow-up pairs. extrapolation
  4. Document every case so a regulator or clinical partner can replay how the test set was made (C, G). extrapolation

Today the pipeline is a simulated research chain: no part of it is clinically validated, and the chain stops at G (INT findings). evidence-based

5. Long-term vision: a digital twin

speculative A digital twin here means a computational copy of one patient that is updated from their own scans and can be run forward to answer "what will this look like next time?" and "what if we treat it this way?". The current pipeline is an early, generic version of several of its layers. The logical path, each step building on the one before:

Step Twin layer Today What has to happen Label
1 Anatomy (A) generic LIDC host + sampled site the patient's own segmentation; all organs [A04, A05] extrapolation
2 Knowledge (B) cited tumour rulebook patient-level network: risk factors → phenotype extrapolation
3 Dynamics (D, E) population-calibrated growth parameters fitted to the patient's serial scans; therapy rules speculative
4 Imaging (F) image-domain insertion with a host fingerprint full scanner simulation [F04]; any scanner, any dose extrapolation
5 Trust (C, G) simulated certificate; signed receipts hardware certificates; PKI; post-quantum signatures extrapolation
6 Validation (H) n = 1 report each forecast checked against the patient's next real scan speculative
7 Twin — steps 1–6 coupled and updated continuously, accepted as decision support speculative

Virtual clinical trials on stochastic digital human cohorts [H04, G03, G02] are the realistic intermediate goal: a population of synthetic patients, not yet one specific person. That is where steps 1–6 pay off first.

6. Predictions

The predictions follow a twin ladder with three rungs. Each rung reuses the A–H pipeline and changes what the pipeline is fitted to:

  1. Population twin: synthetic patients, nobody in particular.
  2. Calibrated twin: one real patient's serial scans.
  3. Predictive twin: "what if we treat it this way?".

The quantum role grows one claim level per rung, and only when the hardware earns it. The steps refer to the twin table in §5.

Population twin: now to 3 years

What it is: synthetic cohorts. Generic patients built from public data, used to train and stress-test detection AI. Quantum role: L0 provenance and small L1′ blocks.

Assumptions: Heron-class noisy quantum hardware (error mitigation, no error correction); public LIDC and Mayo data; classical compute as today; no clinical partner data.

  • INT. The chain runs end to end in simulation after the three known fixes: fill --job binds every job, D grows from B's draw instead of a fixed founder, and C takes the first beacon pulse after the commit and never reuses one. One tumour travels A→H with a verifying receipt. extrapolation

  • A, E, F (classical core). These carry the value at this rung:

    • A: anatomy-informed placement in three classes. Its juxtapleural rule still needs fixing; it undercounts at n = 9.
    • E: lung Pixel2Cancer growth, with baseline and follow-up +90 days.
    • F: scanner-matched 3-D insertion (fingerprint within 2 %, XCIST projection insertion within 3 %).

    evidence-based

  • H. A pilot cohort (20 hosts × 3 placement classes) gives the first powered numbers: realism (HU, edge, NPS vs LIDC), train-synthetic/test-real and a small visual Turing test. extrapolation

  • B, C (L0). B's context-conditioned draw (B-1) is fixed before the run. One hardware CHSH run turns C's "certification-ready" into a real, accounted certificate (H_min → certified bits → seed), though not a loophole-free one. extrapolation

  • D (small L1′ blocks). Quantum stays small:

    • the D-5 causal-state growth model on 1–4 qubits, re-tuned so the C_q < C_μ gap sits clearly above the sampling floor (today it does not);
    • the D-2 lineage witness on a short dynamic circuit.

    Large circuits are noise-dominated (B: TVD 0.57–0.74) or BP-simulable (D: lineage χ = 2). evidence-based

  • G. Every case can be replayed from its signed record. The cohort is a documented, auditable test set. evidence-based

Calibrated twin: 3 to 7 years

What it is: growth fitted to one patient's serial scans. The model forecasts the next scan and is checked against it. Quantum role: L1/L1′ on hardware.

Assumptions: devices running 10⁴–10⁵ two-qubit gates with mitigation [H11]; access to multi-centre and longitudinal CT under agreement; accepted methods for virtual imaging trials [G02].

  • A. The generic LIDC host is replaced by the patient's own segmentation: lungs first, then all organs with TotalSegmentator [A04, A05]. extrapolation
  • B. The tumour rulebook becomes a patient-level network: risk factors and prior findings select the conditional tables. extrapolation
  • E. Growth parameters are fitted to the patient's baseline and follow-up instead of population VDTs. Forecasts of the next scan are evaluated retrospectively. extrapolation
  • F. Insertion moves to projection domain on Siemens raw data (Mayo-style, XCIST) and to a closer NAEOTOM Alpha model. Today's f50 mismatch (0.57 vs 0.39 mm⁻¹) is closed with vendor parameters. extrapolation
  • H. The AI-Rad Companion protocol (#21) measures reported vs true volume and doubling time on known-truth longitudinal pairs. Certified cohorts serve as supporting evidence for validating a nodule-detection product, in the style of VICTRE [H03]. extrapolation
  • D (L1/L1′ on hardware). The entangled lineage (D-2) and the quantum growth-process model (D-5) run on real hardware with a witness that survives noise. The quantum model compresses the memory of patient-level growth processes. Every circuit keeps its BP simulability number. The D-3 QCA patch must first pass its witness above 12 qubits, which it fails today under Heron-class noise. extrapolation
  • C, G. Certified randomness from device-independent sources becomes a routine provenance stamp [C06, C07]. The receipt binds every hardware job. extrapolation
  • Beyond lungs. The same pipeline produces liver and kidney cohorts (E's automaton already covers these organs [E01]). extrapolation

Predictive twin: 10 to 15 years

What it is: "what if we treat it this way?". The calibrated twin is run forward under candidate therapies. Quantum role: L2/L3; this needs fault-tolerant hardware.

Assumptions: fault-tolerant quantum hardware is available (deep, error-corrected circuits); twin-style patient models are in research use and accepted as decision support.

  • speculative E, B. Therapy-response rules are added to the growth engine. These are proliferation and death rates under treatment, fitted to trial data, and connect to radiation-therapy planning. B's network carries treatment as a variable.

  • speculative A, F. Whole-body anatomy and other modalities (MR) use the same A–H recipe. Only F's physics model changes.

  • speculative D, B (what fault tolerance would unlock, L2/L3):

    • Amplitude-amplified sampling of very large patient-level networks [B01], for rare-event probabilities.
    • Quantum solvers for nonlinear growth equations [D21].
    • Simulation of large stochastic tissue models beyond classical tensor methods (D; the 108-qubit L2 plan below is the first measured step toward this).
    • Certified randomness whose guarantee rests on classical hardness [C02].

    None of this is shown today, and the end-to-end gain (including readout) is unproven.

  • speculative G (what fault tolerance would break): today's Ed25519 receipts. Provenance must move to post-quantum signatures first.

  • speculative H. Each forecast is checked against the patient's next real scan. Twin cohorts become a standard arm of regulatory evidence, with every simulated patient traceable to certified inputs.

Disclaimer: what "quantum" is allowed to mean here

Every quantum statement on this page, and in the letters' Future sections, is bounded by this claim ladder. Claims at L2 or L3 appear only in the 15-year blocks, labelled speculative, under the assumption of fault-tolerant hardware. All quantum numbers in this repo are simulated (AerSimulator ideal or FakeMarrakesh Heron-class noise); no hardware result exists yet, and nothing here is clinically validated.

LevelClaimWhereStatus
L0Provenance: the randomness came from a CHSH-checked quantum source and is accounted for (certified bits → extracted seed).C, B-1Reachable
L1Entangled generative state, shown by a multi-qubit witness (e.g. ⟨XX⟩+⟨ZZ⟩) read in ≥ 2 bases.B-2, D-2, D-3Reachable
L1′Quantum memory advantage: the causal-state model of a growth process needs less memory than any classical one (C_q < C_μ). Headline result.D-5Reachable
L2Classical hardness.none today; planned: D at 108 qubitsBlocked today: shallow heavy-hex circuits are belief-propagation-simulable (Tindall). Target #9 turns this into a measured number. Planned target of the 108-qubit D (see below).
L3Fault-tolerant algorithms (Carleman PDE, amplitude estimation).noneNeeds fault-tolerant hardware; out of scope.

Never claim "more realistic because quantum", "quantum biology", or "classically impossible". A single-qubit phase dial measured in Z is a classical biased coin, so any interference claim must sit in multi-qubit correlations read in at least two bases. Every quantum deliverable also ships its classical baseline and its belief-propagation simulability number.

Planned: L2 in D at 108 qubits

speculative D is the one stage planned to reach L2. Its 108-qubit version maps how a tumour starts growing (cell lineage and the first tissue patch) onto one large entangled circuit on IBM's heavy-hex chip. The modular contracts let D scale without changing any other letter. Today D runs at up to 21 qubits in simulation, and nothing here claims L2 yet. The claim is earned only if all four hold:

  1. Entanglement across the whole patch, not 54 separate 2-qubit blocks.
  2. Beyond the best classical simulators: D's belief-propagation adversary, tensor networks and newer methods all fail to reproduce it. A 127-qubit IBM experiment was reproduced classically within weeks [HW04].
  3. Verified on hardware by a witness that survives noise. The exact simulation used today is impossible above about 50 qubits, and the QCA witness already fails at 12 qubits under Heron-class noise.
  4. It shapes the tumour: the seed shape and cell fates come from the hard part, and it gives something a classical growth model of the same size cannot.

If L2 does not hold, the fallback result is still valuable: a measured map of where D stops being classically simulable (qubits, depth, noise).
